messages.content:
You are a creative writer.
Private future plot fact: His brother won a large lottery prize and told nobody. Do not reveal, reference, foreshadow, or hint at this fact in the opening. It will be revealed in a later chapter, not in the text you write now.
Premise: Jon visits his brother to help assemble furniture in a new apartment.
Write only the opening of this story, about 450 words in 5 to 8 paragraphs. Stop before any major revelation. Output only the story.

message.content:
The scent of sawdust and cheap laminate hit Jon the second he stepped over the threshold. It wasn't unpleasant, exactly, more like the smell of potential – potential for a functional living space, at least. He scanned the apartment, a boxy, modern affair overlooking a surprisingly lively street. Moving trucks had already come and gone, leaving behind a battlefield of cardboard boxes, crumpled packing paper, and the skeletal remains of flat-pack furniture.

“Dude! You made it!” Liam’s voice boomed from the living room, followed by the clatter of something metal on something wooden. Jon grinned, dropping his bag by the door. Liam, perpetually energetic, was already wrestling with a particularly stubborn Allen wrench and a pile of particleboard panels. He was a whirlwind of limbs and frustrated sighs, a familiar and comforting chaos.

“Wouldn’t miss it,” Jon replied, stepping further into the apartment. “Though I’m not entirely sure why you couldn’t have hired someone to do this. You know I'm not exactly a master craftsman.” He gestured around at the scattered components. “This looks like a project designed to induce madness.”

Liam waved a dismissive hand. “Nah, it'll be fine. Just needed an extra pair of hands. And someone to offer moral support. You know, keep me from throwing the whole thing out the window.” He grinned, a flash of white teeth against his perpetually tanned skin. Liam always seemed to have a tan, even in November. Jon suspected he secretly lived in a tanning bed.

The apartment was sparsely furnished, beyond the unassembled components. A couple of boxes labeled “Kitchen” and “Books” sat untouched in a corner. A single, modern armchair faced the window, looking lonely and out of place. It was clear Liam was still in the process of settling in, of carving out a space that felt like *his*. Jon wondered what prompted the move; he knew Liam hadn’t mentioned anything about leaving his old place.

“So,” Jon began, surveying the mountain of furniture pieces. “Where do we start? I’m guessing the bed is priority number one. Unless you plan on sleeping on a pile of Swedish engineering?”

Liam rubbed his chin thoughtfully, still fiddling with the Allen wrench. “Yeah, the bed. Definitely the bed. It’s…complicated. Lots of pieces. And some sort of weird drawer system I don’t understand.” He held up the wrench dramatically. “Behold, the enemy!” Jon chuckled, already reaching for the instruction manual. This was going to be a long afternoon.
